mainTopic: Eye blemishes in a בכור: הריס, דק, חלזון and נחש, תבלול, and the tests for constant pale spots and constant tears
overview: The גמרא explains the eye blemishes listed in the משנה. הריס is the eyelid. Two ברייתות disagree about whether a sunken or a floating דק is a מום, and the גמרא settles this by the cataract's color: a black דק counts when sunken and a white דק counts when floating, like ברקא. A story about the elder רבי שמעון בן יוסי לקוניא shows that חלזון and נחש are one permanent blemish, and it raises the rule that a scholar's ruling for himself is accepted only if he taught it beforehand. The משנה's תבלול follows רבי יוסי, who holds there are no blemishes in the white of the eye, and the גמרא gives the reasons for both רבי יוסי and רבי מאיר. A new משנה about constant pale spots and constant tears is shown to follow רבי יהודה, once its missing words are filled in. The גמרא then works out the three-month moist-then-dry fodder test, asks without resolving whether each fodder must be fed in its own season, and sets the amount at a dried fig. A question from ארץ ישראל about that amount continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is the הריס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the word הריס in the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the הריס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for the meaning of a word from the משנה, הריס. This sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed a הריס that was pierced, damaged, or split as a blemish, but it never said what part of the eye the הריס is. Before we can apply the rule, we need to know what body part we are talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
A word from the משנה for a part of the eye

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the 'haris'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word הריס in the משנה's list of eye blemishes

steps.title: רב פפא: the outer barrier of the eye
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that הריס means the outer line, or wall, of the eye, which is the eyelid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is the outer line of the eye.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question: the הריס is the outer barrier of the eye, meaning the eyelid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses an Aramaic phrase that pictures the eyelid as a wall standing guard around the eye. So damage to the eyelid counts as a blemish in the eye area.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The outer line of the eye.
phrases.notes: He means the eyelid, which works like a wall around the eye.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא תּוֹרָא בָּרָא דְּעֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הריס is the eyelid, the outer barrier of the eye

steps.title: A sunken cataract is a blemish, a floating one is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words דק תבלול and brings a ברייתא: a sunken דק is a מום, but a floating דק is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A דק (cataract), a תבלול.' The חכמים taught: A sunken cataract is a blemish; a floating one is not a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words in the משנה, דק and תבלול, and brings a ברייתא that sets a rule for when a דק counts as a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא splits the דק into two kinds. One is sunken into the eye itself and counts as a מום. The other floats on top of the eye and does not count. This rule is the starting point that the next steps will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A cataract, a film on the eye
Another eye blemish listed in the משנה

phrases.english: 'A cataract, a tevallul.'
The Sages taught:
A sunken cataract is a blemish,
a floating one is not a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן דַּק מְשׁוּקָּע הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next term in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sunken דק is a מום; a floating דק is not

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a different ברייתא teaches the reverse, that a floating דק is a מום and a sunken one is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't the opposite taught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. Another ברייתא says exactly the reverse of the one just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ברייתות seem to clash on the same case. One says sunken is a blemish. The other says floating is a blemish. The גמרא now needs a way to fit them together.

phrases.english: But isn't the opposite taught?
phrases.notes: The other ברייתא says that sunken is not a blemish and floating is a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא gives the reverse ruling for the same two cases, so the two sources contradict each other

steps.title: One is about the black part, one about the white part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the first ברייתא is about a דק in the black part of the eye and the second is about one in the white part.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is in the black, that one is in the white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to settle the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different part of the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the two sources deal with different places, they no longer clash. The first ברייתא, where sunken is a blemish, is about the black part. The second, where floating is a blemish, is about the white part.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; no contradiction
Black (the dark part of the eye)
White (the white part of the eye)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is in the black,
that one is in the white.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא בַּשָּׁחוֹר הָא בַּלָּבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by location in the eye
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be talking about the same place in the eye
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ברייתא is about the black part and the second is about the white part

steps.title: There are no blemishes in the white part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer: it is known that there are no מומין in the white part of the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are no blemishes in the white!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. A known rule says the white part of the eye cannot have blemishes at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nothing in the white part ever counts as a מום, the second ברייתא cannot be talking about the white part. So the answer of step 5 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: There are no blemishes in the white part of the eye

phrases.english: But there are no blemishes in the white!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the second ברייתא is about the white part of the eye
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are no blemishes in the white part, so a ברייתא calling something there a blemish makes no sense

steps.title: A white cataract versus a black cataract
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. Both ברייתות are about the black part of the eye, but one is about a white דק and the other about a black דק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: this one is about a white cataract, that one is about a black cataract.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its first answer and offers a new one. The difference is the color of the cataract, not the part of the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both ברייתות are about the black part of the eye, so the rule about the white part is no problem. The second ברייתא, where floating is a blemish, is about a white דק. The first, where sunken is a blemish, is about a black דק.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two answers. The first answer was about WHERE in the eye (black part or white part). The final answer is about the COLOR of the cataract itself, and both cataracts sit in the black part.

phrases.english: Rather:
this one is about a white cataract,
phrases.notes: This is the second ברייתא, where floating is a blemish.

phrases.english: that one is about a black cataract.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא בְּדוּק לָבָן הָא בְּדוּק שָׁחוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of step 5, which step 6 knocked down
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by the color of the cataract
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was the part of the eye, black or white
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are in the black part; a black דק is a blemish when sunken, and a white דק is a blemish when floating

steps.title: Support from יאשיה of אושא, with the memory aid ברקא
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports from יאשיה of אושא the exact rule of step 7: a black דק is a blemish when sunken, a white דק is a blemish when floating. The memory aid is ברקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר בר חנה said: יאשיה from אושא told me: A black cataract that is sunken is a blemish; floating, it is not a blemish. A white cataract that is sunken is not a blemish; floating, it is a blemish. And your memory aid: ברקא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that says exactly what the new answer said, so the answer is backed up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יאשיה spells out all four cases. A black דק is a blemish when sunken, not when floating. A white דק is the reverse. The memory aid ברקא is an eye disease where white patches float on the eye and count as a blemish, which reminds you that a floating white דק is a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: יאשיה from the town of אושא
An eye disease with floating white patches

steps.whatToRemember: A black דק is a מום only when sunken. A white דק is a מום only when floating, like ברקא. This settles the two clashing ברייתות.

phrases.english: As Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
Yoshiya from Usha told me:

phrases.aramaic: דַּק שָׁחוֹר מְשׁוּקָּע — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם,
phrases.english: A black cataract that is sunken is a blemish,
if floating, it is not a blemish.
A white cataract that is sunken is not a blemish,
if floating, it is a blemish.
And your memory aid: barka.
phrases.notes: ברקא is an eye disease where white spots float on the eye and count as a blemish, so floating white is a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה סָח לִי יֹאשִׁיָּה דְּמִן אוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer of step 7
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the ברייתות split between a black דק and a white דק
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר בר חנה quoting יאשיה from אושא
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the final practical rule for checking a בכור's eye: the color of the cataract decides whether sunken or floating is the blemish.

steps.title: Are the snail and the snake one blemish or two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words חלזון, נחש, and עצב and asks whether חלזון is the same as נחש or a separate blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A snail, a snake, and a berry.' A question was asked: Is the snail the same as the snake, or perhaps it means a snail or a snake?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words in the משנה and raises an open question about how to read them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists growths over the pupil shaped like a snail, a snake, or a berry. The question is whether 'snail snake' is one blemish, a snail-shaped growth that is also called a snake, or two separate blemishes. The answer depends on how we read the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Snail (a snail-shaped growth over the pupil)
A question was asked before them

phrases.english: 'A snail, a snake, and a berry.'
phrases.notes: These are words from the משנה, about growths in these shapes that cover the pupil. This text prints עָצָב here. The usual text of the משנה reads עֵנָב, 'a berry', and that is the reading translated.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Is the snail the same as the snake,
or perhaps it means a snail or a snake?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ חִלָּזוֹן הוּא נָחָשׁ אוֹ דִלְמָא חִלָּזוֹן אוֹ נָחָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next term in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חלזון and נחש in the משנה are one blemish or two separate blemishes

steps.title: An elder teaches that חלזון is the same as נחש
steps.stepSummary: Through רבה בר בר חנה, the גמרא brings a story. רבי שמעון בן יוסי לקוניא said that חלזון is a permanent blemish and is the same as the נחש mentioned by the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבה בר בר חנה said that רבי יוחנן בן אלעזר told him: There was an elder in our neighborhood named רבי שמעון בן יוסי לקוניא. I had never passed in front of him. Once I did, and he said to me: Sit, my son, sit. This חלזון is a permanent blemish, and one may slaughter the animal because of it. And this is the נחש that the חכמים spoke about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9 by telling a story. In the story, an elder says outright that חלזון and נחש are the same blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 asked whether the משנה's חלזון and נחש are one blemish or two. The elder's words 'this is the נחש that the חכמים spoke about' settle it: they are the same blemish with two names. He also adds that it is a permanent blemish, so the בכור may be slaughtered because of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'snail': a blemish in the eye shaped like a snail
Literally 'snake': a blemish in the eye listed in the משנה
A permanent blemish, which permits slaughtering a בכור

steps.whatToRemember: חלזון and נחש are one blemish. It is a permanent blemish, so the בכור may be slaughtered because of it.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rabba bar bar Ḥana says:

phrases.aramaic: סָח לִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Elazar told me:
There was a certain elder in our neighborhood,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹסֵי לָקוֹנְיָא שְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Yosei Lakonya was his name,
and in all my days I never passed in front of him.
Once I did pass in front of him,
and he said to me: Sit, my son, sit.
This snail-blemish is a permanent blemish,
phrases.notes: He is pointing at a חלזון in the eye of a בכור that was right there in front of them.

phrases.english: so one may slaughter the animal because of it,
and this is the snake-blemish that the Sages mentioned.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חלזון and נחש are the same blemish, and it is a permanent blemish.

steps.title: How a scholar can have his own בכור permitted
steps.stepSummary: The elder adds that a person may not judge blemishes on his own animal. But he may teach the הלכה to his students, and then they can rule for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though the חכמים said that a person may not examine blemishes for himself, he may still teach the הלכה to students, and the students may rule for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The elder explains why he taught this הלכה just then. He wants his students to be able to permit his own בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that you cannot judge the blemish on your own בכור. The elder found a way around this that the rule allows: he teaches the law, and his students apply it to his animal. That is why he told רבי יוחנן בן אלעזר to sit and listen.

keyTerms.meaning: A person may not examine and permit blemishes on his own animal
Teaches or issues a halachic ruling

phrases.english: And even though the Sages said:
A person may not examine blemishes for himself,
he may still teach the halacha to the students,
and the students may rule for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the elder's words from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar may not permit his own בכור, but he may teach the הלכה to students who then rule for him.

steps.title: A scholar's ruling for himself is accepted only if said beforehand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the elder's method with רב הונא's rule. When a scholar issues a ruling that helps himself, we listen only if he said it before the case came up.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא: Any תלמיד חכם who comes with a ruling, if he said it before the case happened, we listen to him. If not, we do not listen to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the story. It looks like the elder made up his ruling only once his own animal needed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule worries that a scholar might bend the law for his own benefit. The elder taught about חלזון just when his own בכור had one. So it seems his students should not have relied on him.

keyTerms.meaning: We listen to him and accept his ruling

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: But doesn't Rabbi Abba say that Rav Huna says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁמּוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה וּבָא,
phrases.english: Any Torah scholar who comes issuing a halachic ruling,
phrases.notes: He means a ruling that affects his own case.

phrases.english: if he said it before the incident,
we listen to him,
and if not,
we do not listen to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method described in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The students' reliance on the elder's ruling for his own בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling seems to have been said only when the case came up, so by רב הונא's rule it should not be accepted.

steps.title: The elder had taught this ruling all along
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the elder had been teaching this ruling from the start, before his own case came up.
steps.simpleTranslation: He too had been teaching this ruling from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the story. The elder's ruling was not new, so רב הונא's rule does not block it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא only rejects a ruling that first appears when the scholar needs it. The elder had always taught that חלזון is a permanent blemish. So there is no suspicion, and his students could rely on it.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, from the beginning

steps.whatToRemember: A scholar's ruling that helps himself is accepted only if he was teaching it before the case arose.

phrases.english: He too
had been issuing this ruling from the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיהוּ נָמֵי מוֹרֶה וּבָא הֲוָה מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The elder made up the ruling only when his own בכור needed it.
steps.terutzMaskana: He had taught it all along, so רב הונא's rule does not apply.

steps.title: Whose view is the משנה's definition of תבלול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's definition of תבלול as a white line that cuts through the iris. Then it asks which תנא this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a תבלול? A white line that cuts across the iris. Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה and asks whose opinion it follows. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה counts only white entering the dark part as תבלול. It does not mention dark entering the white. That suggests the משנה follows a specific opinion, and the גמרא wants to know whose.

keyTerms.meaning: An eye blemish: a white line running into the dark part of the eye
The colored ring around the pupil (the iris)

phrases.english: What is a tevallul?
A white line that cuts across the iris.
Whose opinion is our mishna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה after the חלזון discussion ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the משנה's definition of תבלול follows.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יוסי: no blemishes in the white
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יוסי. A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר counts both white entering black and black entering white as blemishes, but רבי יוסי counts only white entering black.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יוסי, as a ברייתא teaches: White entering the black, or black entering the white, is a blemish. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says: White entering the black is a blemish. Black entering the white is not a blemish, because there are no blemishes in the white of the eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי יוסי as the author of the משנה. It proves this from a ברייתא where רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions only white entering black. That matches רבי יוסי, who says a mark in the white part is never a blemish. רבי מאיר would also count black entering white, so the משנה does not follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: There are no blemishes in the white of the eye

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's תבלול follows רבי יוסי: only white entering the black is a blemish, because nothing in the white of the eye counts as a blemish.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אין מומין בלבן' is the same idea the גמרא used in step 6. Here we see its source: it is רבי יוסי's opinion, and רבי מאיר disagrees.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yosei,
as it is taught in a baraita:
White that enters the black,
or black that enters the white —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: this is a blemish; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: לָבָן וְנִכְנָס בַּשָּׁחוֹר — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם,
phrases.english: White that enters the black is a blemish,
black that enters the white is not a blemish,
because there are no blemishes in the white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יוסי, who holds there are no blemishes in the white of the eye.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rule 'אין מומין בלבן', used earlier in step 6, is רבי יוסי's opinion, and the משנה follows it.

steps.title: רב explains the source for רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב brings a פסוק showing that the white of the eye is called 'the fat of the eye,' not simply 'the eye.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Why does רבי יוסי hold this way? Because the פסוק says 'Their eyes stand forth from fatness.' This shows that the white part is called 'the fat of the eye,' but it is not called simply 'their eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the reason for רבי יוסי, who said only a white line entering the black part counts as תבלול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the תבלול must be 'in his eye.' רב shows from תהלים that the white part has its own name, 'the fat of the eye.' So plain 'eye' means the dark part, and the blemish must reach into the black.

keyTerms.meaning: The fat of the eye, meaning the white part

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי?
phrases.english: Rav said: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?
As it is written: "Their eyes stand forth from fatness,"
the white is called "the fat of the eye,"
but it is not called simply "their eyes."
phrases.notes: So when the תורה says the תבלול is 'in his eye,' it means the dark part. The white line has to enter the black.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural reason for רבי יוסי's view, which was identified in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plain 'eye' in the תורה means the dark part. So תבלול counts only when white enters the black.

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason of רבי מאיר, who counts mixing in either direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks why רבי מאיר holds that both white entering black and black entering white are blemishes. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After explaining רבי יוסי, the גמרא wants to know how רבי מאיר reads the word תבלול in a way that includes both directions.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir, what is his reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the other side's reason after Step 16 explained רבי יוסי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי מאיר's broader definition of תבלול.

steps.title: תבלול means something that mixes up the eye
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns from the word itself: תבלול means something that mixes (מבלבל) the eye, in either direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the word 'תבלול' mean? Something that mixes up the eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר reads the word תבלול as coming from 'mixing.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any mixing of white and black is a mix-up of the eye, whichever color enters the other. So רבי מאיר does not limit it to white entering black.

keyTerms.meaning: An eye blemish where white and black colors mix

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי: only white entering black, because plain 'eye' means the dark part. רבי מאיר: any mixing, because תבלול means 'mixing.'

phrases.english: What is the meaning of the word "tevallul"?
Something that mixes up the eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר learns from the word itself that any mixing of white and black is a blemish.

steps.title: משנה: constant pale spots and constant tears
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists pale spots and constant tears as blemishes, and says pale spots are 'constant' if they last eighty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Pale spots and tears that are constant are blemishes. Which pale spots count as constant? Any that lasted eighty days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with two more eye blemishes. It also defines when pale spots are permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a permanent blemish lets a בכור be slaughtered. So the משנה needs a test to tell a passing problem from a lasting one. For pale spots, the test is lasting eighty days.

keyTerms.meaning: Pale white spots on the eye
Constant tears, meaning the eye keeps running

phrases.english: MISHNA: Pale spots and tears that are constant.
Which are the pale spots that are constant?
Any that lasted eighty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with new blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pale spots that last eighty days are a permanent blemish.

steps.title: רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס: check three times
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס adds that the spots must be checked three times within the eighty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס says: We check it three times within the eighty days.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא in the משנה adds a requirement about how to confirm the eighty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough that spots were seen at the start and at the end. They must be found at three checks during the eighty days to show they really stayed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥananya ben Antigonus says:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים בְּתוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים יוֹם.
phrases.english: We examine it three times within eighty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a checking requirement to the eighty-day rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pale spots must be found at three checks within the eighty days.

steps.title: The food test for constant tears
steps.stepSummary: Tears are a permanent blemish only if they continue after the animal eats moist food and then dry food.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are constant tears. Suppose the animal ate moist and dry food from a rain-watered field, or moist and dry food from an irrigated field, or ate the dry food and then the moist. In those cases it is not a blemish. It counts only when the animal eats the moist and afterwards the dry, and the tears still do not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the test for whether running tears are permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is given food as a remedy. Only one order counts as a real test: moist first, then dry. If the tears continue after that, the blemish is permanent. Any other way of eating does not prove anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Rain, here a field watered only by rain

steps.confusionAlert: Eating both kinds of food is not enough. The order matters. Only moist first and then dry is the real test.

phrases.english: And these are the constant tears:
If it ate moist and dry fodder from a rain-watered field,
or moist and dry fodder from an irrigated field,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אָכַל הַיָּבֵשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַלַּח —
phrases.english: or it ate the dry and afterwards the moist,
it is not a blemish,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיֹּאכַל הַלַּח וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַיָּבֵשׁ.
phrases.english: unless it eats the moist and afterwards the dry.
phrases.notes: The idea is that the tears still don't stop even after this proper food remedy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the second blemish named in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tears are permanent only if they continue after the animal eats moist fodder and then dry fodder.

steps.title: Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking whose view it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eighty-day rule for pale spots is not agreed on by everyone. So the גמרא wants to identify which side the משנה follows.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Whose opinion is the mishna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the משנה's eighty-day rule follows.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר requires only forty days for pale spots, while רבי יהודה requires eighty, like the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches: constant pale spots need forty days, and constant tears need eighty days. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: pale spots need eighty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, and it brings a ברייתא to show the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, pale spots become permanent after forty days. For רבי יהודה, they need eighty. Our משנה says eighty, so it matches רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: Pale spots: רבי מאיר says forty days, רבי יהודה says eighty days. Our משנה follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught in a baraita:
Constant pale spots: forty days,
and constant tears: eighty days,
this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: חֲוַרְוָור — שְׁמוֹנִים יוֹם.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda says: pale spots, eighty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 22 using a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who requires eighty days for pale spots, against רבי מאיר's forty.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's test for permanent tears
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: for רבי יהודה, fodder from an irrigated field is not a real test. Eating dry fodder and then moist fodder is not enough either. The tears count as a blemish only if they continue after the animal eats dry fodder following moist fodder, and the test runs three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the constant tears: if the animal ate moist and dry fodder from an irrigated field, or ate dry fodder and then moist fodder, it is not a blemish. It becomes a blemish only if the animal eats dry fodder after moist fodder and is still not healed. The test lasts three months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the same ברייתא from the last step. Now it gives רבי יהודה's rules for when tears count as a permanent blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the animal must eat moist fodder first and then dry fodder. If the tears still don't stop, the blemish is proven. Fodder from an irrigated field does not prove anything, and eating dry before moist does not count either.

keyTerms.meaning: constant tears (an eye that keeps tearing)
an irrigated field (watered by hand or by channels, not by rain)

phrases.english: And these are the constant tears:
phrases.notes: This is still the ברייתא, giving רבי יהודה's view.

phrases.english: If it ate moist and dry fodder
from an irrigated field,
or if it ate dry fodder
and afterward ate the moist fodder,
it is not a blemish
until it eats dry fodder after the moist fodder,
and this period lasts three months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא brought in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tears are a permanent blemish only if they continue after the animal eats moist fodder and then dry fodder (not from an irrigated field), over three months.

steps.title: The משנה mentions both kinds of fields
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. The משנה lists fodder from rain-watered fields and fodder from irrigated fields together, as if they are the same. רבי יהודה says irrigated fodder does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה taught both: moist and dry fodder from a rain-watered field, and moist and dry fodder from an irrigated field!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the claim from step 23 that the משנה matches רבי יהודה. The משנה seems to treat both kinds of fields the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said only irrigated fodder fails as a test, which means rain-watered fodder does work. But the משנה lists both kinds together. So how can the משנה be following רבי יהודה?

keyTerms.meaning: rain (here: a field watered only by rain)

phrases.english: But we learned both of them:
phrases.notes: He means both kinds of fields appear in our משנה.

phrases.english: it ate moist and dry fodder from a rain-watered field,
moist and dry fodder from an irrigated field!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that the משנה matches רבי יהודה, using the ruling just quoted in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (step 23) that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats rain-watered and irrigated fodder alike, but רבי יהודה distinguishes between them.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing some words. Read properly, it says rain-watered fodder is a valid test and irrigated fodder is not. Even with rain-watered fodder, the order must be moist first and then dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means: if the animal ate moist and dry fodder from a rain-watered field, it is a blemish. From an irrigated field, it is not a blemish. Also with rain-watered fodder, if it ate dry and then moist, it is not a blemish until it eats dry after moist.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. It says the משנה left some words out, and it fills them in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the missing words filled in, the משנה separates the two fields exactly like רבי יהודה: rain-watered fodder counts, irrigated fodder does not. It also adds that even with rain-watered fodder, the order must be moist and then dry. So the משנה matches רבי יהודה after all.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what it is teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה made the two fields equal. After the missing words are filled in, rain-watered fodder proves the blemish and irrigated fodder does not.

phrases.english: It is missing words
and this is what it is teaching:
if it ate moist and dry fodder from a rain-watered field,
this is a blemish;
from an irrigated field, it is not a blemish;
and with rain-watered fodder too,

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל יָבֵשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָכַל לַח —
phrases.english: if it ate dry fodder and afterward ate moist fodder,
it is not a blemish,
until it eats dry fodder after the moist fodder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the משנה (חסורי מחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה treats rain-watered and irrigated fodder alike, against רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה, read with its missing words, treats rain-watered fodder as a valid test and irrigated fodder as not valid, like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows רבי יהודה: only rain-watered fodder, eaten moist and then dry, proves the tears are a permanent blemish.

steps.title: Four months, not three?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's 'three months.' רב יצחק בר אשיאן said the moist period is אדר and ניסן and the dry period is אלול and תשרי. That makes four months.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it lasts three months.' Is that so? But רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיאן: אדר and ניסן are the moist period, and אלול and תשרי are the dry period!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the last words of the ברייתא, 'three months,' and challenges them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two months of moist fodder plus two months of dry fodder adds up to four months. That clashes with the ברייתא's three.

phrases.english: 'And it lasts three months.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the end of the ברייתא from step 24.

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא — וְהָא רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: But isn't it taught, but didn't רב אידי בר אבין
phrases.notes: Two openings sit side by side here. Some versions say 'it is taught' and others say 'רב אידי said'; the meaning is the same.

phrases.english: say that רב יצחק בר אשיאן said:
Adar and Nisan are the moist period,
Elul and Tishrei are the dry period!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the length of the test given in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that the test lasts three months.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יצחק בר אשיאן names two moist months and two dry months, which totals four months, not three.

steps.title: Only half of ניסן and half of תשרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording of רב יצחק בר אשיאן's statement. The moist period is אדר and half of ניסן, and the dry period is אלול and half of תשרי. That adds up to three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: אדר and half of ניסן are the moist period; אלול and half of תשרי are the dry period.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading רב יצחק בר אשיאן's statement a little differently, so the two sources agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each period is a month and a half, not two months. A month and a half of moist fodder plus a month and a half of dry fodder is three months, just like the ברייתא says.
steps.whatToRemember: The three-month test is a month and a half of moist fodder (אדר and half of ניסן) plus a month and a half of dry fodder (אלול and half of תשרי).

phrases.english: Say instead:
Adar and half of Nisan are the moist period,
Elul and half of Tishrei are the dry period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the statement (אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each period is two full months, four months in total.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each period is a month and a half, three months in total, matching the ברייתא.

steps.title: Must each kind of fodder be fed in its own season?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether moist fodder is fed in the moist season and dry fodder in the dry season, or whether both are fed during the moist season.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Do we feed moist fodder in the moist season and dry fodder in the dry season? Or maybe we feed both moist and dry fodder during the moist season?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question about how to run the moist-then-dry fodder test. This question sets up the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the order is moist first and then dry. The open question is timing. Option one is to follow the real seasons, which spreads the test across the year. Option two is to run the whole test during the moist season, using dry fodder saved from last year.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a real open question)

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Is it moist fodder at the time of moist fodder,
phrases.notes: "Moist time" is the end of the rainy season, when the grass is fresh.

phrases.english: and dry fodder at the time of dry fodder,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: לַח וְיָבֵשׁ בִּזְמַן הַלַּח?
phrases.english: or perhaps: moist and dry, both at the time of moist fodder?
phrases.notes: In this option, the dry fodder would be food left over from last summer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the fixed reading of the משנה (moist and then dry) and the three-month time frame, and asks how the timing actually works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the moist-then-dry test follow the real seasons, or can both stages happen during the moist season?

steps.title: Trying to prove it from the months for moist and dry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer from רב יצחק בר אשיאן's statement that אדר and ניסן are the moist period and אלול and תשרי are the dry period.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיאן: אדר and ניסן are the moist period, and אלול and תשרי are the dry period.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement that seems to answer the question: each type of fodder has its own months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If moist fodder belongs to אדר and ניסן and dry fodder belongs to אלול and תשרי, it sounds like each one is fed in its own season. That would support the first option.

keyTerms.meaning: The spring months: the moist season
The late-summer months: the dry season

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for Rav Idi bar Avin said
that Rav Yitzchak bar Ashiyan said:
phrases.notes: This is the same statement the גמרא just adjusted to half-months (Step 28).

phrases.english: Adar and Nisan are moist,
Elul and Tishrei are dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of Step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That moist fodder is fed in the moist season and dry fodder in the dry season.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יצחק בר אשיאן's statement assigning moist to אדר and ניסן and dry to אלול and תשרי.

steps.title: The months may describe the food, not the feeding time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: maybe the months tell us which crop to use, and we feed the אלול and תשרי crop during אדר and ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps we feed the animal the produce of אלול and תשרי during אדר and ניסן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof. The statement about the months does not have to mean when the animal eats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "אלול and תשרי are dry" may only name where the dry fodder comes from: last year's late-summer crop. That food can be stored and fed later during אדר and ניסן. So the statement fits the second option too, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps (used to push away a proof)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not answered here. The גמרא only shows that this source does not prove anything. Both options are still possible.

phrases.english: Perhaps the produce of Elul and Tishrei
we feed it during Adar and Nisan!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question from Step 29 is left without an answer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The months in the statement may describe which season's crop is used, not when the feeding happens.

steps.title: How much fodder is given?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much fodder the animal must be fed for the test.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much do we feed it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new detail of the test: the amount of food. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know the kind and order of the fodder, the גמרא wants the amount. Without a set amount we could not know whether the test was really done.

phrases.english: And how much do they feed it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the timing question and opens a new question about quantity.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of fodder needed for the test.

steps.title: The amount is the size of a dried fig
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי פנחס בן ערובא, says the animal is fed the size of a dried fig.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי פנחס בן ערובא: the size of a dried fig.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the amount is a כגרוגרת, the size of a dried fig.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a clear measure for the test. But it does not yet say whether this amount is for the whole day or for each meal. The next step raises exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of a dried fig

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Pinchas ben Arova:
The size of a dried fig.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן עָרוֹבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal is fed an amount the size of a dried fig (כגרוגרת).

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל they asked what the fig-size amount means
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that in ארץ ישראל they asked: is the dried-fig amount given at the first meal of each day? The question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they asked: Does it mean the size of a dried fig at the first meal,
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reports a question that was asked in ארץ ישראל about רבי יוחנן's answer. The sentence is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the amount is a כגרוגרת, but not when it is given. The first option is a fig-size amount at the first meal of the day. The other option comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: They ask, they raise a question
In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not finished here. Wait for the other side of the question before deciding what it means.

phrases.english: Rava said:
They ask in the West:
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is the printed text; the word in square brackets, "they ask," is the corrected reading. "The West" means ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Is it the size of a dried fig at the first meal,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question about the dried-fig amount given in Step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dried-fig amount is given at the first meal of each day, or in some other way (the second option comes later in the text).
